front: State the ASE 2010 Rudski normal RVEDV index for men and women.
back: Men: ≤ 87 mL/m². Women: ≤ 74 mL/m². (Both larger than LV EDV indices — reflecting the crescent RV shape.)

front: What is 'RV free-wall strain' and what abnormal cutoff is used?
back: RV free-wall longitudinal strain measured by speckle tracking. Normal is more negative than −20% (average of 3 segments). Values less negative than −20% (e.g., −15%) suggest RV dysfunction.

front: Give three key echo findings of ARVC/D on Task Force Criteria.
back: 1) RV outflow tract diameter enlarged (> 32 mm end-diastole). 2) Regional RV free-wall dysfunction (aneurysm or dyskinesis). 3) Reduced RV FAC (< 33%) or RV EF (< 45% by cMRI). Also epsilon wave and T-wave inversions V1–V3 on ECG.

front: Why is TAPSE reduced after cardiac surgery even if intrinsic RV function is preserved?
back: Pericardial adhesions restrict longitudinal (base-to-apex) motion of the RV; TAPSE reflects longitudinal displacement, so it drops even though radial and circumferential contraction may be preserved.

front: State two Doppler indices that assess RV function independent of geometry.
back: 1) RIMP (Tei index) by PW Doppler (> 0.43 abnormal) or TDI (> 0.54 abnormal). 2) RV S′ velocity by TDI (< 9.5 cm/s abnormal).

front: How does RV pressure overload differ from RV volume overload in septal motion timing?
back: Pressure overload (PAH, PS): septum flattens throughout systole → D-shaped LV in systole. Volume overload (severe TR/PR, ASD): septum flattens in diastole only (LV is normal shape in systole).
